agent_context.content: Design a progressive 4-month low-impact workout plan (Gym + Home)
I need to clarify a few key details about your fitness goals before designing the 4-month progressive plan. This will ensure the workout plan is tailored to your needs and realistic.

1. Returning after a break – I used to jog 5Ks but haven’t trained since my daughter was born 18 months ago.  
2. Main goal is dropping the 18 lbs I still have from the pregnancy, plus getting my core strength back (diastasis feels almost shut).  
3. Gym: 2 weekdays (Tue/Thu) while she’s at daycare; weekends are home-only.  
4. Home stuff: 8-lb and 15-lb dumbbells, two 20-lb kettlebells, green & purple resistance bands, yoga mat, and a sturdy doorway pull-up bar.  
5. Can give you 45 min on gym days, 30–35 min at home before naptime ends.  
6. No injuries, but my left knee feels crunchy going downstairs—avoid deep weighted squats/lunges for now.  
7. Love swimming and Pilates; hate long steady-state cardio on machines (bores me to death).

Perfect. I have all the context I need to design a comprehensive 4-month progressive plan. You're returning postpartum with specific equipment, time constraints, and preferences. I'll create a structured progression that:

1. Respects your knee limitation (avoid deep weighted squats/lunges initially)
2. Prioritizes core rebuild (diastasis recovery)
3. Leverages your love of swimming and Pilates
4. Fits your 45-min gym window (Tue/Thu) + 30-35 min home sessions (weekends)
5. Incorporates fat loss through varied intensity, not boring steady-state
6. Progresses intelligently over 4 months from low-impact foundation to stronger capacity

I'm ready to generate the detailed plan now.
